Subject: Procurement kickoff & demo scheduling with StellarNet - proposed times

Hi Alex and Priya,

Thanks again for the interest in Redwood — excited to get StellarNet into our onboarding flow. Per our call earlier this week, we'd like to schedule two things:

1) A 45-minute product demo / architecture walkthrough with your engineering team (AE + SE + customer engs)
2) A short procurement kick-off (30m) with your procurement and security teams to align contract/timeline and required evidence (SOC2, encryption, data retention)

Proposed windows next week (PDT):
- Tue 24 Mar, 10:00–11:00
- Wed 25 Mar, 14:00–14:45
- Thu 26 Mar, 09:00–09:45

Attendees from our side: myself (AE), Priyom (SE), Rafael (Customer Success lead), Stephanie (Legal/Privacy backup). Please let me know which slot works and who from StellarNet should join each session (engineering, procurement, security).

I attached a short vendor onboarding checklist and a draft SOW to speed procurement review.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Hi Marissa,

Thanks — appreciate the clear options. Quick notes:
- Engineering: I can pull in our platform eng (Priya) and our lead systems engineer, Jordan Patel. Either Wed 25 at 14:00 or Thu 26 at 09:00 works best.
- Procurement: Our procurement lead (procurement@stellarnet.com) is available Thu 26 Mar 11:00–12:00 PST or Fri 27 Mar 09:00–10:00 PST.
- Security: They want the onboarding checklist beforehand and will likely have a short questionnaire; happy to share contact details if you need.

Can we do the demo on Wed 25 at 14:00 and procurement kickoff on Fri 27 at 09:00? If so, please send invites.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — I’ll take the demo. Draft agenda (45m):
- 0–5m: Introductions and success criteria (Marissa)
- 5–25m: Architecture walkthrough (Priyom)
- 25–35m: Integration patterns & data flows (Priyom + Alex)
- 35–45m: Q&A and next steps (All)

I’ll also bring a slide with recommended quantization/batching settings and estimated token cost for the sample workload if you can share expected prompt lengths.
